name: From a named piece of work to its design
outcome: The product owner runs three plays on a business intent and gets a slice to test, a plan with one epic and one story for each feature, and an eval that no build is given; a check flags each build session that read the evals folder, and the flag is recorded in that build run's evidence.

surface.name: the Claude Code command line
surface.user_action: runs /shape-slice, then /shape-plan, then /shape-eval on a business intent, then runs the check that shows no build play's inputs name the evals folder, and finds the flag of a build session that read it in that build run's evidence

why_this_order: The slice must exist before its plan, and the plan's epic and stories before the eval that reads them. The check of fn-898 comes last, because it can only be tested when the evals folder holds an eval that a build must not be given.

left_out.what: Running the eval after the build (also on Griffin)
left_out.why: The approved design puts it out of scope (798/specs/design.md line 31), and fn-798 lists it as out of scope (fn-798/feature.md line 29).

left_out.what: Blocking a read of the evals folder by a hook (#893)
left_out.why: Story #898 only flags the read and does not block it; blocking is the guardrails work (#893), out of scope in the design (line 31-32).
The product owner dropped encryption and #828 on 2026-10-26 (798/specs/design.md lines 7-10): everything stays in plain text.

left_out.what: Showing the flag anywhere other than the build run's evidence: in the run's close report, or as drift checks and evidence warnings in Griffin
left_out.why: The product owner said the flag is recorded under evidence for now, and that the drift checks and evidence warnings that show it will be built in Griffin later (answer to Q-flag-1).

left_out.what: Changing the proof line of business intent 788 that says no builder can read the eval
left_out.why: The product owner said yes to the new words (Q-proof-1: 'No builder is given the eval, and a check flags each build session that read the evals folder.'), but this slice changes no word of a confirmed intent page: /shape-slice writes an intent page only when the model has none. The brief names the change as still to be made on the intent page.

left_out.what: The design, build, test or validation of an epic (#819)
left_out.why: The intent's Must not excludes it (bi-788.md line 18); so the slice has no build play of its own, and the check of fn-898 treats every play, skill and agent that builds the software, and every context sub-agent it starts, as a build play; only /shape-slice, /shape-eval and the eval may name the evals folder (the product owner's answer to Q-builders-1).

decisions.question: Which features does the slice hold?
decisions.answer: fn-795, fn-818 and fn-798, kept as they are, and the new feature fn-898 under cap-shape-eval: the build is given the business intent, never the eval; a check flags each build session that read the evals folder, and records the flag in that build run's evidence.

decisions.question: In which order are the features built?
decisions.answer: fn-795, then fn-818, then fn-798, then fn-898.
